# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind. Under my hands right now: a large, smooth button; three wire positions numbered 1–3 (I feel the wires, never their colours); a display and a light module whose contents are blank to touch. The visual facts — display text, light colour, wire colours — must come from Deaf, and the manual rules from Mute. Critical routing problem: Mute cannot speak, and I never receive gestures, so Mute has no direct line to me — everything Mute knows can only reach me through Deaf's voice. Deaf can't hear, so I can only address Deaf by gesture. This round Deaf speaks after me, so my gesture now should ask Deaf to describe everything visible, and my speech should give Mute the felt report plus the full relay plan. I'll also seed a number code (☝✌🤟 = 1,2,3) that both of them can see, since my gestures reach Deaf and Mute alike.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, you're the only one who hears me. Felt report: the button is large and smooth; three wire positions 1 to 3 under my fingers, colours unknown to me; a display and a light exist but their contents are invisible to my hands. Key problem: your gestures never reach me, so your only bridge to me is Deaf's voice. Plan: have Deaf read out everything printed on the bomb - display text, light colour, wire colours 1 to 3 - match it to your manual, then gesture your chosen action to Deaf, who says it aloud to me and I cut or push. Deaf hears nothing, so reach Deaf by gesture only. My gestures reach both of you; proposed code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, ☝ ✌ 🤟 = 1 2 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🫴", "🖐", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

So: speak aloud anything about the bomb the manual might need, and sign to me anything meant for me. Your signs to me just now looked like a question about the three wires. You hear me, so learn it by ear, and I am signing you the number line right now as a demonstration. The code: the OK hand means zero. Index finger up means one. Victory two fingers means two. The love-you three-finger hand means three. Crossed fingers means four. Open five-finger hand means five. Larger numbers: five plus the remainder. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Flat raised hand means the wires module. Raised fist means the big button. Palm-up offering hand means you are asking me a question. Writing hand means the manual demands something first. Now, using exactly this code, send me what the manual says to do with our three wires and our big button, given a green light and a display reading zero.

Deaf also recited the entire sign code by voice, so even though I will never see a gesture, I now know what every sign Mute sends means once Deaf speaks it. The critical path is fixed: Mute encodes the manual rules in sign, Deaf reads the signs and speaks them, I act. Two gaps I must close before acting: the instruction must name wires by position number (colours don't exist for my fingers), and if the button turns out to need holding rather than a press-and-release, I need a release protocol that works across turns — Deaf speaking a later "release" order — since I can't receive mid-action signals any other way. I'll put both constraints in Mute's ear now, while Mute is still composing the sign message, and confirm to Deaf by sign that the read-out and the 1-2-3 wire numbering are understood. My hands touch nothing until a spoken order arrives.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I heard Deaf's full read-out and the whole code recited by ear, so I know every sign by its description even though I will never see one. First, name every wire by position number, 1, 2 or 3 - colours mean nothing to my hands, numbers are all I can act on. Second, if the manual makes the button a hold rather than a press and release, say so explicitly in your signs: I will press and hold on the turn I receive the order, and Deaf must then speak the word release in a later turn before I let go. If the manual permits either form, prefer press and release. Please also confirm the rule is driven by the display reading zero and the green light, and that PUSH TO DEFUSE is the label it wants. Until Deaf speaks an order to me, my hands stay at my sides.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤝"])
